title: 446. Trigonometry & Periodic Models: Determining a Sinusoidal Rule from a Graph
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Sine rule from a graph through the origin
questions.learningObjective: Choose between sine and cosine from the behaviour of a graph at the origin.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph passes through the origin and rises to its first maximum value \(3\) at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\). Its minimum value is \(-3\) and its period is \(2\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The graph has amplitude \(3\), midline \(y=0\), and period \(2\pi\). A graph that starts on its midline at \(x=0\) and rises matches the sine: \(3\sin 0=0\) and \(3\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=3\). The rule \(y=3\cos x\) would give the value \(3\) at \(x=0\), not \(0\).
questions.hint: Check the value of each candidate at \(x=0\).

questions.concept: Cosine rule from a graph starting at a maximum
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a cosine graph from a maximum on the vertical axis.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has a maximum point at \((0,2)\), minimum value \(-2\), and period \(2\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(2\) and the midline is \(y=0\). A graph that starts at its maximum when \(x=0\) matches the cosine: \(2\cos 0=2\). The rule \(y=2\sin x\) would give \(0\) at \(x=0\).
questions.hint: A cosine graph starts at a maximum; a sine graph starts on the midline.

questions.concept: Coefficient of the variable from the period
questions.learningObjective: Determine the coefficient of the variable from the period shown by a graph.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph passes through the origin going upward, has amplitude \(1\) and midline \(y=0\), and completes one full cycle between \(x=0\) and \(x=\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The period is \(\pi\), so \(\frac{2\pi}{B}=\pi\) and \(B=2\). The rule is \(y=\sin 2x\). The rule \(y=\sin\frac{x}{2}\) has period \(4\pi\), four times too long.

questions.concept: Amplitude and midline from a graph
questions.learningObjective: Determine amplitude and midline from the extreme values shown by a graph.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has maximum value \(5\) and minimum value \(1\), has period \(2\pi\), and crosses its midline going upward at \(x=0\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(\frac{5-1}{2}=2\) and the midline is \(y=\frac{5+1}{2}=3\). Starting on the midline and rising matches a sine, so \(y=2\sin x+3\). Check: its maximum is \(3+2=5\) and its minimum is \(3-2=1\). The rule \(y=3\sin x+2\) has range from \(-1\) to \(5\).
questions.hint: Compute half the difference and the average of the extreme values.

questions.concept: Period from a maximum and the next minimum
questions.learningObjective: Use the distance from a maximum to the next minimum to find the period.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has a maximum point at \((0,4)\), and the next minimum point is at \((2,-4)\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The distance from a maximum to the next minimum is half a period, so the period is \(2\cdot 2=4\). Then \(B=\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}\), and \(y=4\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)\). Check: at \(x=2\), \(4\cos\pi=-4\). The rule \(y=4\cos(\pi x)\) has period \(2\) and would give \(4\cos 2\pi=4\) at \(x=2\).
questions.hint: A maximum and the following minimum are half a period apart.

questions.concept: Graph starting on the midline and falling
questions.learningObjective: Recognise a reflected sine from a graph that falls from the origin.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph passes through the origin going downward, has amplitude \(2\), midline \(y=0\), and period \(2\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: A sine graph through the origin that falls first has a negative coefficient: \(y=-2\sin x\). Check at \(x=\frac{\pi}{2}\): \(-2\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=-2\), a minimum, as expected for a graph that falls first. The rule \(y=2\sin x\) rises first.
questions.hint: Check the value of each candidate a quarter period after the origin.

questions.learningObjective: Recognise a reflected cosine from a minimum on the vertical axis.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has a minimum point at \((0,-3)\), maximum value \(3\), and period \(2\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(3\) and the midline is \(y=0\). A cosine graph that starts at its minimum has a negative coefficient: \(y=-3\cos x\) gives \(-3\cos 0=-3\). The rule \(y=3\cos x\) starts at the maximum value \(3\).
questions.hint: Evaluate each candidate at \(x=0\) and compare with the given point.

questions.learningObjective: Assemble a cosine rule from several features of a graph.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has a maximum point on the \(y\)-axis, amplitude \(2\), midline \(y=-1\), and period \(\pi\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: A maximum at \(x=0\) suggests a cosine with positive coefficient \(2\). The midline gives the constant \(-1\). The period \(\pi\) gives \(B=\frac{2\pi}{\pi}=2\). So \(y=2\cos 2x-1\). The rule with \(\frac{x}{2}\) has period \(4\pi\).

questions.concept: Phase shift from a midline crossing
questions.learningObjective: Determine the phase shift of a sine from the position of an upward midline crossing.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has amplitude \(1\), midline \(y=0\), and period \(2\pi\). It crosses its midline going upward at \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The graph of \(y=\sin x\) crosses its midline going upward at \(x=0\). Here that point has moved to \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\), a shift of \(\frac{\pi}{4}\) to the right, so \(y=\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\). Check: \(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=0\). The other rule gives \(\sin\frac{\pi}{2}=1\) at \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\), a maximum.
questions.hint: Substitute \(x=\frac{\pi}{4}\) into each candidate; the correct rule must give \(0\) there.

questions.concept: Full rule from a maximum and a minimum point
questions.learningObjective: Determine amplitude, midline, period, and phase shift from two extreme points.
questions.question: A sinusoidal graph has a maximum point at \((1,6)\), and the next minimum point is at \((4,-2)\). Which rule fits the graph?
questions.explanation: The amplitude is \(\frac{6-(-2)}{2}=4\) and the midline is \(y=\frac{6+(-2)}{2}=2\). Half a period is \(4-1=3\), so the period is \(6\) and \(B=\frac{2\pi}{6}=\frac{\pi}{3}\). A cosine with its maximum moved to \(x=1\) gives \(y=4\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{3}(x-1)\right)+2\). Check: at \(x=4\), \(4\cos\pi+2=-2\). The other rule uses the full difference \(8\) as amplitude and the minimum as midline.
questions.hint: Find the amplitude and midline from the two \(y\)-values, and half the period from the two \(x\)-values.
